corrections.why: The 1934 Bulletin reports the steel tower as newly completed in April 1934 and describes the 1929 light as a small acetylene light; Lighthouse Friends gives the 1929 wooden tower's height as 32 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Both dates are right for different structures: the 1929 date is the first, small acetylene light (Bulletin 1934); the 1934 date is the steel tower that replaced it. Wikidata's 1934 and the USLHS record's 1929 describe these two structures.
Lighthouse Friends puts his arrival at 1938. The archive lists him as first assistant from 1938 to 1942 and principal from 1942 to 1960, so both are consistent: 1938 was an assistant post.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) Site purchase: Lighthouse Friends gives 31 December 1928 for the 58-acre purchase; the 1934 Bulletin says the site was acquired in 1929. The story reports both. (2) Tower height: the 1934 Bulletin says the new steel tower is 110 feet high (checked on the rendered page image, PDF p. 7; the OCR reads the same, and the story reports the disagreement). The archive gives 125 ft from base to lantern center (156 ft focal height); Lighthouse Friends says roughly 125 ft above ground. (3) Current status: the archive marks the light as an active aid. The station record cites Rowlett's Lighthouse Directory for deactivation in 2019, but that directory was not read, so the story does not use it. The 2025 Light List, Volume VI (local copy data/raw/uscg_light_list/V6.txt) has no Cape Kumukahi entry. The story says the sources do not settle whether the light is shown now. (4) Keepers Frederick E. Nihoa (1936-1942) and Joseph Brown (1946-1948) are named only by Lighthouse Friends; the archive does not list them. Verify against NARA registers before publishing as roster rows. (5) Pestrella's 1963 retirement (Wikipedia lead, Ke Ola) is not used; no source I read gives it. (6) The Evening Star quotes are OCR text. The 31 January item is an AP report datelined Kapoho Village, 30 January, so the story dates the Civil Defense statement to 30 January. The 20 January item names Seismologist Jerry P. Eaton, whom the story does not name. (6b) The fiscal-year labels were corrected: each Commissioner report is for the fiscal year ended 30 June of its label; the estimates in it are for later fiscal years. (7) Not read: the Smithsonian GVP report (403), the archived USCG Historian page (403), the Big Island Now 2021 notice (body not in cache), the Carteret County News-Times of 8 July 1960. Roster matched by name and position (0.48 km). Newspaper search for 1929-1934 Hawaii papers returned no hits. No photos searched.
